notes: Community pack, roadmap Phase 1 candidate. 5 tracks x 10 themes x 5 grade bands = 250 blocks. Expanded by tools/generate_pack.py.

tracks.name: Drawing, colour and the seeing eye

themes.theme: Drawing what is there, not what you know
themes.description: Observation over symbol — contour, negative space and the practice of trusting the eye against the brain's shorthand.
themes.transfer_check: Produce an observational drawing of a real object using contour and negative-space methods, alongside the from-memory version that shows the difference.

themes.theme: Light and the shape it makes
themes.description: Value, shadow and form — how five tones turn a circle into a sphere.
themes.transfer_check: Render one real lit object in a five-value study where the light direction is unmistakable.

themes.theme: Colour: the wheel and the why
themes.description: Hue, value, saturation and the relationships — complement, analogue, temperature — that make palettes work.
themes.transfer_check: Mix and apply a deliberate limited palette for one image, and name the relationship rule the palette obeys.

themes.description: Framing, thirds, leading lines and the deliberate placement of what matters — the picture as a directed path.
themes.transfer_check: Recompose one weak image (yours or found) two different ways and explain which compositional move fixed it.

themes.description: Proportion, gesture and the quick pose — drawing people as structures in motion rather than assembled features.
themes.transfer_check: Complete a set of timed gesture drawings from a live or video model, with the last showing measurably better proportion than the first.

themes.description: Pencil, ink, paint, digital — what each medium wants to do, and choosing the tool for the intention.
themes.transfer_check: Execute the same small subject in three media and articulate what each medium gave and refused.

themes.description: Studying artists you love, the master copy as a tool, and the line between learning from and passing off.
themes.transfer_check: Make one labelled master copy, then one original piece applying its lesson, and state exactly what was borrowed.

themes.description: Daily pages, bad drawings on purpose, and the sketchbook as a private gym rather than a gallery.
themes.transfer_check: Keep a daily sketchbook for two weeks and present it with your own annotation of what improved and what to attack next.

themes.description: Describing before judging, the question behind the criticism, and hearing feedback as data rather than verdict.
themes.transfer_check: Give a structured critique of a peer's work (describe, analyse, suggest) and revise one of your own pieces from critique received.

themes.description: When a piece is done, preparing work for a wall or a feed, and the small courage of putting it where people look.
themes.transfer_check: Finish, title and publicly display one work — physical or online — and document one response you received.

themes.description: Active listening — picking out instruments, structure and production choices instead of letting music be wallpaper.
themes.transfer_check: Map one song's full structure and instrumentation from listening alone, verified against a second listener or source.

themes.theme: Pulse, rhythm and the body's clock
themes.description: Beat, subdivision and groove — internalising time before any instrument is touched.
themes.transfer_check: Clap or play three distinct rhythm patterns against a steady beat, holding each through a distraction.

themes.description: Matching pitch, carrying a melody, and why 'tone deaf' is almost always untrained rather than untrue.
themes.transfer_check: Sing or play back a short unfamiliar melody accurately after limited hearings, alone or in unison.

themes.theme: Harmony: notes that agree and argue
themes.description: Chords, progressions and the four chords under half the songs you know.
themes.transfer_check: Play or program a common progression and identify it by ear inside two real songs.

themes.description: Posture, tone production and the practice loop — beginning an instrument with habits that will not need undoing.
themes.transfer_check: Perform a simple piece on your instrument with assessed posture and tone, plus your practice log for the fortnight behind it.

themes.theme: Reading and the other ways in
themes.description: Notation, tab, chord charts and ear — the entry systems into written music and when each serves.
themes.transfer_check: Learn one short piece from written form (notation, tab or chart) without a recording, then verify against one.

themes.description: Ensemble craft: listening across, entering together, and the discipline of being quiet enough.
themes.transfer_check: Rehearse and perform one piece with at least one other musician, holding your part against theirs.

themes.theme: Making a track in the box
themes.description: Loops, layers, arrangement — producing a piece of music in software from silence to bounce.
themes.transfer_check: Produce and export a one-minute original track with at least four intentional layers, and walk through your arrangement choices.

themes.theme: The song: words that are music
themes.description: Lyric, hook and form — writing a song that says one thing and lands it.
themes.transfer_check: Write and perform (or demo) one original song with a defined hook, and state the single thing it says.

themes.description: Traditions, borrowings and the histories inside genres — listening to music as the record of the people who made it.
themes.transfer_check: Trace one genre you enjoy back through two of its source traditions with listening examples, and present the chain.

themes.description: What is in, what is out, and where the camera stands — every shot as a decision about what the viewer may know.
themes.transfer_check: Photograph one subject five ways — distance, angle, framing — and explain what each frame lets the viewer believe.

themes.description: Finding, shaping and waiting for light — why the hour and the window beat the expensive camera.
themes.transfer_check: Shoot the same subject in three different lighting conditions and rank the results with the reasons visible in the images.

themes.description: Why audiences forgive bad video and abandon bad audio — mic placement, room noise and the recorded room tone.
themes.transfer_check: Record the same short scene with camera audio and with a placed microphone, and present the difference.

themes.description: Questions that open people, listening while operating, and the ethics of what your subject didn't realise they said.
themes.transfer_check: Record a five-minute interview with a real subject — framed, lit, mic'd — and cut its best two minutes honestly.

themes.description: Selection, order and rhythm — how meaning is made in the cut, and made differently by a different cut.
themes.transfer_check: Cut the same footage into two versions with different meanings or moods, and screen both.

themes.description: Short-form structure: hook, turn, payoff — the discipline of a complete story inside a feed's attention span.
themes.transfer_check: Make a ninety-second piece with an identifiable hook, turn and payoff, and test it on a viewer who owes you nothing.

themes.description: Staging, cropping, colour and AI generation — where enhancement ends and deception begins, and the disclosure that keeps trust.
themes.transfer_check: Take one of your own images or clips, push it past the honest line deliberately, and mark the exact edit where it stopped being true.

themes.theme: Faces, consent and the right to be unfilmed
themes.description: Filming people: consent, minors, public space law and the human ask behind the legal minimum.
themes.transfer_check: Produce a short piece involving other people with documented consent, and state where law and courtesy diverged.

themes.description: Formats, thumbnails, captions and what each platform's machine rewards — distributing work without being distributed by it.
themes.transfer_check: Publish one piece properly prepared for two different platforms, and compare what each did to it and for it.

themes.description: Projects over posts: series, consistency and the portfolio that shows a maker rather than a lucky upload.
themes.transfer_check: Plan and complete a three-piece series with a stated through-line, presented as a single body of work.

tracks.name: The stage and the spoken word

themes.description: Stance, stillness, breath and the eyes — occupying a space before saying anything in it.
themes.transfer_check: Hold a stage or room entrance, pause and first line before an audience, with feedback on presence alone.

themes.theme: The voice that reaches the back
themes.description: Breath support, projection, pace and the pause — a voice that carries without shouting.
themes.transfer_check: Deliver the same passage to the back of a real room quietly failing and then correctly projecting, confirmed by a listener there.

themes.theme: Saying words you did not write
themes.description: Text work: meaning first, memory second, and making a written line sound like it occurred to you.
themes.transfer_check: Perform a memorised minute of someone else's text with intention choices you can defend line by line.

themes.description: Accepting offers, building with a partner and failing cheerfully in public — improvisation as trained generosity.
themes.transfer_check: Play three improv structures with a partner before observers, sustaining accept-and-build throughout.

themes.theme: The character who is not you
themes.description: Body, voice, want — building someone else from observable choices rather than costume.
themes.transfer_check: Present the same short scene as two distinct characters, changed by observable physical and vocal choices only.

themes.theme: The speech with a job to do
themes.description: Persuading, honouring, explaining — occasion speeches structured for their actual purpose and audience.
themes.transfer_check: Write and deliver a three-minute speech for a real occasion and purpose, judged against whether it did its job.

themes.description: What stage fright is physiologically, the preparation that shrinks it, and performing well while still afraid.
themes.transfer_check: Perform after deliberately rehearsing a personal pre-performance routine, and report what the nerves did and what you did back.

themes.description: Rehearsal discipline, hitting cues, and the offstage professionalism that companies are actually built on.
themes.transfer_check: Rehearse and perform a group piece hitting every entrance and cue, with the stage manager's log as evidence.

themes.theme: The audience is part of the show
themes.description: Reading a room, riding laughter and silence, and recovering the moment that just died.
themes.transfer_check: Perform one piece twice for different audiences and describe, specifically, what you adjusted between them and why.

themes.description: The production itself: space, tickets, tech, front of house — the unglamorous machine around every performance.
themes.transfer_check: Take one named production role (stage manager, tech, producer, FOH) through a real event and deliver its checklist complete.

tracks.name: Craft, design and the made object

themes.description: Users, constraints and the brief — design as solving a person's problem rather than decorating your own.
themes.transfer_check: Write a real design brief from interviewing an actual user, with constraints and success criteria they confirm.

themes.description: Many cheap versions before one dear one — ideation as volume, and the courage to bin the favourite.
themes.transfer_check: Produce ten distinct concept sketches for one brief, and defend which two advance and why the favourite died.

themes.theme: Materials: what wants to be what
themes.description: Wood, fabric, clay, paper, plastic — properties, joins and the material honestly matched to the job.
themes.transfer_check: Choose and justify materials for one real object, and demonstrate the appropriate joining technique for your choice.

themes.description: Marking out, tolerances and the accumulating error — precision as respect for the future assembler and user.
themes.transfer_check: Make a multi-part object where the parts actually fit, with your marking-out shown and measured against tolerance.

themes.theme: The tool and the respect it demands
themes.description: Hand and power tools: capability, technique and the safety rules written in other people's scars.
themes.transfer_check: Demonstrate safe, correct technique on three tools appropriate to your level, including one you were newly trained on.

themes.theme: Type, layout and the designed page
themes.description: Graphic design's core: hierarchy, alignment, contrast, whitespace — making information look like what it means.
themes.transfer_check: Redesign one genuinely bad real-world document or poster, and annotate each change with the principle it applies.

themes.theme: The prototype that answers a question
themes.description: Building the cheapest thing that tests the riskiest assumption — prototyping as inquiry, not miniature manufacture.
themes.transfer_check: State one design's riskiest assumption, build the minimum prototype that tests it, and report the answer.

themes.description: Modifying and mending the made world — the confidence to open, alter and improve objects you own.
themes.transfer_check: Repair or usefully modify one real broken or inadequate object, documenting before, process and after.

themes.description: Why some objects delight and others infuriate — analysing the designed world's hits and crimes.
themes.transfer_check: Analyse one excellent and one terrible everyday object, and specify the design decisions responsible for each.

themes.theme: Making for someone, start to finish
themes.description: The commission: brief, design, make, deliver — one complete arc ending in an object in its user's hands.
themes.transfer_check: Complete a real commission for a real person from brief to handover, with their assessment of it against the brief.
